rounds.text: Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd demonstrates exceptional compounding capability, evidenced by compounded profit growth of 117% over 3 years and 75% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E18]. This robust financial performance is underpinned by elite returns on capital, including an ROE of 24.0% and an ROCE of 22.7% [E11, E12], comfortably outperforming sector benchmarks where sector median ROCE is just 6.1% [E65]. Operating efficiency is concurrently expanding, with operating margins surging to 33% in March 2026—a 21 percentage point increase over three years [E22]—supported by a declining opex-to-AUM ratio from 19.9% to 18.0% [E76]. Valuation metrics offer a wide margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow analysis sets intrinsic value at Rs 643 per share against a market price of Rs 374 [E38], leaving a 41.9% margin of safety [E39] while the reverse DCF implies a modest 10.6% growth rate compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E40]. Growth runways remain expansive, backed by management guidance projecting AUM growth upwards of 40% [E66] alongside a rapidly scaling Loan Against Property business now spanning 101 branches across eight states [E72]. Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -461 Cr [E27], resulting in a weak cash conversion of -1.64x against reported profit [E26], alongside a rising debt-to-equity ratio of 1.81x [E30].

Severe cash flow divergence creates an immediate vulnerability, as operating cash flow for March 2026 registered a steep negative outflow of Rs 461 Cr, resulting in a troubling cash conversion ratio of -1.64x against reported profit [E26, E27]. This cash burn is compounded by escalating leverage, with total borrowings surging to Rs 2,429 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 1,562 Cr a year prior, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.81x where obligations comfortably exceed net worth [E30, E32]. Concurrently, insider and institutional confidence is visibly fraying, marked by a negative money flow signal alongside a reduction in promoter ownership down to 23.57% and a drop in domestic institutional holdings to 17.64% [E34, E36, E37]. Operational momentum also exhibits cracks, evidenced by sequential quarterly operating margin compression from 33% to 31% and an inconsistent short-term trend [E23, E25]. Furthermore, management has had to actively retrench by reducing disbursements by 7% and pausing lending across roughly 450 pin codes due to elevated risk warnings flagged in small-ticket loans across the industry [E85, E86]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 21x while demonstrating strong multi-year compounding in sales and profits alongside a high ROE of 24.0% [E1, E12, E15, E18].

Conceded: [E26], [E27], [E28], [E30], [E32], [E34], [E36], and [E37]. While reported operating cash flow was negative for March 2026, the company successfully completed its IPO in May 2026, propelling net worth to INR 2,245 crores and fortifying the NBFC subsidiary's capital adequacy to a robust 40.2% [E81, E82]. This substantial equity infusion of approximately ₹630 crore directly addresses leverage concerns by backing the book with fresh capital rather than reliance purely on debt [E83]. The sequential contraction in quarterly margin by 2 percentage points is minor against a multi-year trend of expanding annual operating margins that rose from 12% to 33% over three years [E22, E23, E24]. Furthermore, the proactive reduction in disbursements by 7% and pausing of lending across 450 riskiest pin codes is not a sign of weakness, but evidence of disciplined risk management and calibrated selection designed to protect asset quality while guiding credit costs down [E86, E87]. Institutional outflows and slight promoter trimming do not negate the fundamental strength of a business delivering a 24.0% ROE and a 100 relative-strength rating [E12, E34, E36, E44].

Conceded: [E81, E82] regarding the capital adequacy rising to 40.2% and net worth reaching INR 2,245 crores following the May 2026 IPO. However, the bull's dismissal of the negative cash flows ignores that operating cash flow was deeply negative at Rs -461 Cr and free cash flow stood at Rs -471 Cr in March 2026, representing a cash conversion of -1.64x against reported profit [E26, E27, E28]. While the bull argues that fresh equity addresses leverage, total borrowings actually surged to Rs 2,429 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 1,562 Cr a year earlier, driving the debt-to-equity ratio to an uncomfortably high 1.81x where debt exceeds net worth [E30, E32, E83]. The bull frames the 2 percentage point quarterly operating margin compression as minor, but it reflects an inconsistent quarterly margin trend over the last two quarters alongside negative institutional money flow and declining domestic institutional holdings from 19.05% to 17.64% [E23, E25, E36, E37]. Furthermore, the bull praises the 7% disbursement reduction and lending pause across 450 pin codes as disciplined risk management, yet this defensive action stems directly from building industry-level stress concentrated in small-ticket loans and multiple-lender borrowers that threatens the company's growth narrative [E85, E86].

Conceded: [E26, E27, E28, E32] regarding negative operating cash flow, free cash flow, and the absolute level of borrowings at Rs 2,429 Cr. However, the bear's alarm over leverage ignores that the net worth has expanded to INR 2,245 crores and capital adequacy in the NBFC subsidiary rose dramatically to 40.2% following the May 2026 IPO and subsequent equity infusion [E81, E82, E83]. While the bear cites a 2 percentage point quarterly margin contraction, this represents a minor blip against a stellar yearly operating-margin trend that has expanded by 21 percentage points over four years to reach 33% [E22, E23, E24]. The bear mischaracterizes the disbursement reduction as a broken growth narrative, whereas management explicitly frames it as calibrated risk selection while tracking firmly on course for over 40% AUM growth and disciplined credit costs [E67, E68, E86]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on institutional outflows and small-ticket stress overlooks the exceptional fundamental profitability evidenced by a 24% ROE and a 5-year profit CAGR of 47% [E12, E16, E52].

Conceded: [E81, E82, E83] regarding the net worth expansion and capital adequacy surge following the IPO. However, pointing to a capital adequacy ratio of 40.2% [E81] does not erase the stark reality of negative operating cash flows of Rs -461 Cr and negative free cash flows of Rs -471 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27, E28], which directly undermine the sustainability of reported profits. While the bull downplays the sequential margin contraction as a minor blip, the quarterly operating-margin trend is explicitly classified as inconsistent over the last two quarters [E25]. Furthermore, dismissing the reduction in disbursements and the pausing of lending across 450 pin codes as mere "calibrated risk selection" [E86] masks the severe industry-level bureau data revealing building stress concentrated precisely in small-ticket loans and multiple-lender borrowers [E85]. Finally, while the bull waves away institutional outflow by citing a 24% ROE [E12], domestic institutions actually cut their stake from 19.05% to 17.64% [E36], and promoters trimmed their holdings while holding a low base of only 23.57% [E34, E53], signaling acute insider and institutional apprehension that a high ROE alone cannot soothe.
